goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

candidates: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 - Removing per-request Init calls drops the "service is stopping" rejection. `Stop` sets `s.initErr = "service is stopping"`. Every handler used to call `s.Init(ctx)`, which returned that error, so requests made after shutdown began were refused. Init now runs only in the constructor, and the per-request calls are gone from Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch and the other handlers. After `Stop`, these handlers keep serving and writing against a backend and search index that are shutting down. Keep a cheap check in the handlers, for example returning `s.initErr` if it is set. Alternatively, add a separate stopping flag and check that.
